Use case: precise-object-edit / ui-mockup. Edit target: the attached Korean mobile employment-card app screenshot. Create ONE high fidelity polished mobile UI design variant, portrait aspect ratio matching the reference. This is a visual UI concept, not a photo of a phone. No device frame, no perspective, no hands. Maintain the reference screen's exact design language and palette: near-white cool gray/lavender background, white card, deep dark navy text, bright warm coral-pink approximately #FF536F / #FF6464 only as in the original, pale gray-blue secondary elements. Absolutely do NOT substitute the earlier teal/ivory palette or add new colors.
INVARIANTS: Preserve the existing job card design and its office photo, company white logo tile, badges "4/4 조건 일치", "정규직", "D-7", company "(주)넥스트커머스", subtitle, title "핀테크 웹 프론트엔드 React 개발자", 2 by 2 gray information block, tags "#React", "#TypeScript", "#유연근무", and footer "공고 상세 정보 보기". Preserve the card's visual proportions and rounded corners/shadow. Preserve back chevron upper left and fixed bottom three-item navigation "일자리 탐색", "나의 매칭", "피드백", with coral selected first tab and count badge 3. The card may be shifted upward slightly to give its new bottom handle enough space, without changing card content design or size disproportionately.
CHANGE: Replace the disconnected bottom coral CTA bar and its "즉시 지원" button with a new bottom-of-card gripping handle/control described below. Remove the far-away top floating "위로 밀어서 넘기기" pill so gesture labels are located right beside the handle. Keep small "이전 공고 되돌리기" below the new control.
GESTURE SEMANTICS: Grabbing handle and pulling DOWN moves the ENTIRE card down and offscreen and applies; pushing UP flips the ENTIRE card and reveals rejection-reason selection on the reverse. This image shows the front-card idle state only. Both directions must be unmistakably explained at the handle with arrows and exact Korean copy. No left/right swipe cues. Do not show a settings toggle, progress bar, horizontally swiping control, or phone home indicator as the handle. Handle has clear grip texture, enough finger-sized hit area, and looks physically connected to the bottom of the card. Explain in nearby small helper text "밀면 사유 선택 · 당기면 지원". Render Korean legibly. No extra dashboards, new features, or illustrations. No written design rationale outside the app.
VARIANT A — INTEGRATED CARD TAB. Integrate a compact rounded coral-tinted tab centered on the bottom edge of the white card, overlapping and protruding like a drawer handle. The tab is about 45% of the card width and 46px tall at 390px viewport; its grip is three short horizontal navy lines with a small centered vertical double-chevron motif. Card surface flows naturally into this tab, visibly attached. Place "↑ 밀어서 넘기기" in muted navy directly above the grip within the upper part of the interaction region and "↓ 당겨서 지원" in bold coral directly below. Keep these labels legible and not overlapping the grip. Below use two small low-emphasis accessible text buttons "↑ 넘기기" and "↓ 지원" in one row, separated by substantial space. This should be the cleanest, simplest variant, strongly tied to the card. A tiny top-right label "A · 카드 연결 탭형" identifies this concept.

VARIANT B — VERTICAL GUIDED SLIDER. Attach a short narrow pale navy-gray vertical rail to the underside center of the card; rail extends downward into the interaction area. Use one round coral grip/thumb in the MIDDLE of the rail with a white six-dot grip pattern, diameter about 46px at 390px viewport. A short connector makes card and rail read as one assembly. There is meaningful travel both above and below the resting thumb. An upward chevron and label "밀어서 넘기기" sit by the upper end of the rail. A downward chevron and label "당겨서 지원" sit by the lower end. Upper and lower direction guides should make the vertical motion unmistakable; include no horizontal track. The labels must not collide with the thumb. It should look like a bidirectional drag affordance, not a quantity slider: no ticks, numbers, percentage or progress fill. Beneath, subtle separate compact buttons "넘기기" and "바로 지원". A tiny top-right label "B · 세로 레일형" identifies this concept.

VARIANT C — WIDE BIDIRECTIONAL PADDLE. Add a wide, touch-friendly paddle integrated into the bottom of the job card, about 80% of the card width and 96px tall at 390px viewport. It is ONE contiguous draggable handle with a narrow obvious central horizontal grip of six dots, not two separate unrelated controls. Its upper region is pale cool-gray with navy text "↑ 밀어서 넘기기"; its lower region uses the reference bright coral with bold white text "↓ 당겨서 지원". Use softly rounded lower corners, a fine divider at the center, a tactile raised central grip crossbar spanning about 35% of paddle width, and continuous visual attachment to the card. The two direction labels vertically bracket the grip so the card manipulation is intuitively up/down. Retain nearby small hint "가운데 손잡이를 잡고 움직여요". This is the most explicit, readable and finger-friendly variant. No separate oversized floating CTA underneath. A tiny top-right label "C · 양방향 패들형" identifies this concept.

VARIANT D — HANGING LOOP HANDLE. Attach a single elegant hollow oval/rounded-rectangle coral loop to the card's lower edge, with two short coral stems joining its upper left and right to the underside of the white card. Flat minimal UI, not realistic fabric or metal. Loop is about 90px wide and 44px tall at 390px viewport with a 6px coral outline, opening filled with background, and small navy grip marks on its lower crosspiece. The loop should feel like a pull handle physically belonging to the card. Place a small navy upward double-chevron and "밀어서 넘기기" directly above the loop, and coral downward double-chevron and "당겨서 지원" directly beneath it. Both direction labels are vertically aligned, NOT left/right. Use very short pale guide arrows just outside the loop to suggest its upward/downward travel. Below this, a quiet pair of small text buttons "↑ 넘기기" and "↓ 지원" allows direct tap actions. This design should be visually distinctive through its airy hollow loop, preserving plenty of white space and a mature minimal aesthetic. A tiny top-right label "D · 고리 손잡이형" identifies this concept.
